sections.title: Musk rose
sections.text: A vigorous, arching rose from southern Iran to Afghanistan, treated by Kew as a scrambling shrub or liana. In cultivation it commonly reaches about 2.5–4 m in both height and spread. Its late-season, musk-scented white flowers are borne in large clusters and reach about 5 cm across; rounded orange-red hips follow.

sections.title: Use and comparison
sections.text: The white clustered flowers and rounded hips in the plate fit this species. Rose hips are used as food in the genus, but a species-specific food or toxicity assessment for R. moschata was not confirmed in the sources consulted.
